actions.description: Pause the simulation clock with /sss_clock_control; /clock holds after at most the regulator's pending 0.01 s step until a client resumes it
actions.name: pause

outputs.description: True once the /sss_clock_control service acknowledged the request
outputs.name: acknowledged

actions.description: Resume clock advancement at an operator-selected speed ratio

inputs.description: Simulation speed ratio for the resumed clock
inputs.name: max_sim_speed

actions.name: resume

outputs.description: True once the /sss_clock_control service acknowledged the request
outputs.name: acknowledged

facts.text: The sim clock advertises rosgraph_msgs/Clock on the absolute /clock topic and std_msgs/Bool on the absolute /sss_clock_is_online topic, both as latched publishers.
TimeServer advertises the absolute /sss_clock_control, /sss_timeclient_register and /sss_timeclient_unregister services.
The clock-control callback sets is_paused_ from the proceed field, changes max_speed_ratio_ and the wall-timer period only when max_sim_speed is nonzero, and always answers success=true.
The speed-regulator wall timer requests and tries a clock update only while the clock is not paused.
The update-clock-request callback stores the client's request and calls try_update_clock without checking is_paused_.
try_update_clock publishes the minimum pending request on /clock only when every time client has a new request and that request is later than the current ROS time.
try_update_clock checks the clients from index 0 and does not publish when any of them, client 0 included, has no new request.
After publishing, try_update_clock clears has_new_request for every client whose request time is at or before the new sim_time_.
The TimeServer constructor registers time client 0 as the simulation speed regulator.
The regulator step speed_regulator_period_ is 0.01 s and its wall timer period is that step divided by max_speed_ratio_.
The node reads max_speed_ratio (default 100) and auto_start (default false) and starts with is_paused_ = !auto_start_.
sim_clock.launch defaults max_speed_ratio to 100, auto_start to true and open_ui to true, and starts clock_ui.py when open_ui is set.
clock_ui.py calls /sss_clock_control with proceed=True from call_start, with proceed=False from call_pause, and with proceed=True and the new max_sim_speed from call_speed_change.
clock_ui.py connects call_start to the Start button, call_pause to the Pause button and call_speed_change to the speed dial's valueChanged signal.
Registering a time client appends it, returns client_id and success=true, and calls try_update_clock.
Unregistering client 0 is refused; a matching nonzero client id is erased and success set true, otherwise success stays false.
The SimClockControl request carries proceed and max_sim_speed, and max_sim_speed 0 keeps the original simulation speed.
The SimClockControl response is a success boolean.
The TimeRequest message carries time_client_id and request_time.
The README describes swarm_sync_sim as a synchronized (lock-stepped) multi-robot swarm simulation platform based on ROS.
The README's first usage step launches sss_sim_env sim_clock.launch with max_speed_ratio and auto_start arguments.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned-response fake that adds a fixed placeholder step on each /clock observation while unpaused; no wall-clock pacing, participant accounting, lock-step scheduling or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS recording transport (event-driven clock control, no simulator)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers /clock, /sss_clock_is_online and /sss_clock_control with canned messages and runs no TimeServer, nodelet manager, ROS graph, time-client network or wall-clock regulator
the clock sample is a placeholder and advances by a fixed test step on each observation while unpaused; the fake cannot establish wall-clock pacing, regulator timing or lock-step determinism
/clock is latched in the clone and the fake returns the held sample while paused; that sample is not fresh stopped-state evidence
the pause flag in the fake only changes the fake's own state; no external time client or update_clock_request path exists in this package

the fake holds /clock at once after a pause, while the clone can still complete the regulator's pending 0.01 s step when time clients request it; the fake's reject_clock_application switch models a reply the clone never sends (its callback always answers success=true)

the shipped sim_clock.launch starts clock_ui.py by default, and its Start button or any speed-dial change sends proceed=true, so a pause, the e-stop's included, holds only while no ROS client resumes the clock; the MHS latch refuses only this driver's commands
while paused, nodes timed on simulated time (the simulated vehicles' timers, the visualizer loops) freeze; nodes on wall time do not

participant registration (/sss_timeclient_register, /sss_timeclient_unregister) and per-client time requests (/sss_time_client/update_clock_request) are NOT COVERED: a single rosbridge binding cannot sequence register, request and wait for /clock, and a registered silent client blocks clock updates
the simulated robots, MAVROS/px4 topics, tello and UGV dynamics, physics stepping, reset, snapshot, restore and rendering are NOT COVERED by this package

operator_required.name: resume
operator_required.reason: the /sss_clock_control callback accepts every nonzero max_sim_speed and the clone states no numeric maximum; the launch value is a configured default, so the operator supplies the site speed-ratio envelope

safe_state.description: The acknowledged /sss_clock_control request sets is_paused_, so the speed regulator (time client 0) stops posting clock requests; as try_update_clock publishes /clock only when every client, client 0 included, has a new request, simulated time advances at most the pending 0.01 s regulator step and then holds, freezing nodes timed on simulated time, until any ROS client, the shipped clock UI Start button or speed dial included, sends proceed=true.
